response.consequence: A user can be wrongly denied access to a resource they are allowed to see for the cache TTL, after a different resource with an ambiguous name/parent split was denied. This is a fail-closed error, not an authorization bypass.
response.explanation: userPermDenialCacheKey builds its key as namespace.perm_uid_action_name_parent. Name and parent are request-controlled and can contain "_". Check(name="a_b", parent="c") and Check(name="a", parent="b_c") therefore produce the same key. A denial cached for one request makes Check return Allowed:false for the other without evaluating permissions. The key also shares the "<ns>.perm_<uid>_<action>" prefix with userPermCacheKey. I did not verify whether cacheWrap shares one keyspace across its caches. If it does, a name/parent that collides with the shape of a permission key could mix stored types.
response.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous because it joins request-controlled fields with "_"
